+# ADR 0001: Increase Pricing Cache TTL
+
+## Context
+
+Our pricing data is fetched from an external service and cached to reduce API calls and improve system responsiveness. The current cache TTL of 900 seconds (15 minutes) requires frequent refreshes from the upstream pricing service. During peak traffic periods, this results in redundant API calls when multiple requests arrive before the cache expires, straining our API quota and adding unnecessary latency to user requests. Analysis shows that pricing information changes infrequently—typically only when promotional periods begin or end, or when our billing team updates rates. The cost of serving stale pricing data for an additional 45 minutes is minimal compared to the overhead of frequent refresh cycles.
+
+The Anthropic prompt-cache mechanism uses a similar 3600-second (1-hour) TTL window for caching model context, which provides a proven reference point for reasonable cache durations in our system. Extending our pricing cache to align with this pattern simplifies operations and reduces the likelihood of cache inconsistencies across different components.
+
+## Decision
+
+We will increase the pricing cache TTL from 900 seconds to 3600 seconds (1 hour). This change applies to all pricing data cached at the application level, including model costs, rate cards, and promotional pricing. Cache invalidation will still occur immediately when pricing updates are published through the admin interface, preserving the ability to push urgent changes without waiting for expiration.
+
+## Consequences
+
+**Positive:**
+- Reduced API calls to the pricing service by approximately 75%, lowering our monthly API usage and associated costs.
+- Improved P99 latency for pricing lookups by eliminating unnecessary network round-trips during cache misses.
+- Simplified cache management logic and reduced operational complexity when reasoning about cache consistency.
+
+**Negative:**
+- Users may see pricing data up to 1 hour stale in edge cases where updates occur without admin intervention (e.g., automatic promotional window activation). This is acceptable given the rare occurrence and business impact.
+- Requires clear communication to the billing and finance teams about the new cache window so they understand the delay between making a pricing change and observing it in production.
+
+**Mitigation:**
+- Implement monitoring to track cache hit rates and TTL effectiveness, alerting on anomalies.
+- Provide admin tooling to manually flush the pricing cache when urgent updates are needed before the 1-hour window expires.
